gemini.rationale: The transaction was structured as a whole-company acquisition where KCG became a wholly owned subsidiary of Virtu, transferring its products and operational processes intact (gap_45 = 0). While top executives exited, continuing employees transferred with the operations, meaning there was no documented structural mismatch between processes and the organization running them at closing (gap_56 = 0).

grok.rationale: The slice structures an all-cash whole-company merger in which KCG survives as Virtu’s indirect wholly owned subsidiary and its customer-facing securities-trading business (market making, agency execution, trading venues) is absorbed intact, so T4 product and T5 processes cross together with no documented product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0). T6 is only partial because the proxy states no continuing role for Company directors or executive officers while extending one-year pay/benefits/severance commitments only to continuing employees, yet those continuing employees and the surviving corporation still move with the operations, so processes are not transferred without an aligning organizational substrate at closing (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: The structural summary describes a whole-company merger in which KCG’s customer-facing securities-trading business was absorbed as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Virtu, with no operational carve-out identified; therefore, the product and its operating processes moved together and gap_45 is 0 [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-17-003764, DEFM14A]. For gap_56, the transaction transferred the operating business but disclosed no continuing role for KCG’s directors or executive officers, while covering only employees who remained employed and expressly flagging employee-retention risk, documenting incomplete organizational alignment alongside the transferred processes at closing [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-17-003764, DEFM14A]. The slice identifies integration and employee covenants but no transitional-services or operating agreement allocating a shared operational substrate, so the documented gap was not contractually absorbed in the specified manner [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-17-003764, DEFM14A].
